name: The Spire
description: The first escalation band above the warm Atrium — a tall, cool spire of cobalt-and-violet stone climbing toward a single bright beacon at its crown. This is the MAPPING-MUTATION band: the cues stay simple TAP cues, but the color->button code (the Xbox default blue=X, green=A, red=B, yellow=Y you learned in the Atrium) is SCRAMBLED per floor, and the scramble deepens as you climb. Floor 1 swaps a single color-pair (one rule bends); floor 2 swaps two pairs; floor 3 runs a three-color cycle; the crown floor is a full DERANGEMENT where no color keeps its home button — the decode is now the whole difficulty, not speed. Hero landmark: the Beacon Obelisk, a faceted violet-cobalt obelisk topped by a bright cyan crystal beacon that you orient by from anywhere in the band. Palette + legibility plan: a deep navy/cobalt/violet stone base kept dark and cool so the bright cyan beacon and accent POP off it (relative-luminance spread well over the 0.3 threshold — the dark stone reads as silhouette, the beacon as light). DISTINCT from its nearest sibling, the Atrium: the Atrium is fully WARM (amber stone, lantern-gold, golden sky) and fully CALM (baseline mapping); the Spire is COOLER, cleaner, and taller — cold cobalt/violet stone against a deep night-blue sky with a cyan beacon instead of a warm gold lantern, and it is the first band that actively subverts the mapping. The mean-palette signatures sit far apart, so the two never blend.
